title: Cost Analysis Template
description: The cost analysis that holds up in front of a CFO — versus the back-of-envelope that turns into a board-deck embarrassment. Five components per feature, scaling curve included. The discipline is honest assumptions: per-user usage distribution is rarely uniform, and the cost surprise is in the long tail.
empty_template_md:
# [Feature] — Cost Analysis
_v[N] · prepared by [AIE] · [date] · for [audience]_

## 1. Headline numbers
_Per-user-per-month cost at current usage. Per-query cost. Total monthly cost at current volume. One line each._

## 2. Cost components
_Breakdown of where the money goes. Typical components: model API (input + output tokens), embedding costs, vector store, compute / orchestration, observability._

## 3. Usage distribution
_Per-user usage is rarely uniform. Median, P95, P99 queries per user per month. The cost calculation should use the actual distribution, not the average — especially if you're pricing for the customer or budgeting for the year._

## 4. Scaling curve
_What does cost look like at 2×, 5×, 10× current usage. Where do the cost-per-query economics change (e.g. switch to a cheaper model? add caching? batch processing?)._

## 5. Key assumptions + sensitivities
_The three assumptions whose negation would materially change the headline. With a sensitivity range (e.g. 'if response length grows by 30%, monthly cost grows by ~25%')._

worked_examples.content_md:
# Customer-KB Assistant — Cost Analysis
_v0.2 · prepared by [AIE] · 16 May 2026 · for: Henrietta Cole (finance) → board prep_

## 1. Headline numbers

- **Per-user-per-month cost (40 daily active users):** ~$1.18
- **Per-query cost (typical):** ~$0.022
- **Total monthly cost (current volume):** ~$47
- **Total annual cost (current volume):** ~$564

## 2. Cost components (per query)

| Component | Cost | % of total |
|-----------|------|------------|
| Generation (Claude Sonnet 4.5, ~3K input + ~400 output tokens) | $0.0162 | 73% |
| Embedding (text-embedding-3-large, ~1 query embedding @ ~50 tokens) | $0.0000065 | <1% |
| Vector store (pgvector on existing infra) | $0 incremental | 0% |
| Compute / orchestration (Lambda invocation, 200ms median) | $0.0008 | 3% |
| Observability (LangSmith traces, ~1 per query) | $0.005 | 23% |
| **Total per query** | **$0.022** | 100% |

## 3. Usage distribution (last 30 days, beta period)

- Median user: 14 queries/month
- P75 user: 38 queries/month
- P95 user: 72 queries/month
- P99 user: 154 queries/month
- Active-user count: 40

_Note: distribution is right-skewed. The top 5 users (12.5% of base) account for ~38% of total queries. Cost-per-user above is volume-weighted, not per-user-average._

## 4. Scaling curve

| Scale | DAU | Queries/month | Monthly cost | Per-user-per-month |
|-------|-----|---------------|--------------|---------------------|
| Current | 40 | ~2,100 | $47 | $1.18 |
| 2× usage | 80 | ~4,200 | $94 | $1.18 |
| 5× usage | 200 | ~10,500 | $235 | $1.18 |
| 10× usage | 400 | ~21,000 | $470 | $1.18 |

**Cost-per-query stays linear** through 10×; no caching, batching, or model-tier changes are needed at that scale. Above 1,000 users we'd revisit:
- Caching the top ~20 FAQ patterns (estimated 30% query reduction, ~$0.007/query savings on cached queries)
- Routing simple queries to Claude Haiku 4.5 (rough ~5× cost reduction on routed queries; ~15% of queries currently look simple enough)

## 5. Key assumptions + sensitivities

- **Average response length: 400 tokens.** If response length grows by 30% (e.g. we ask the model to provide more detail), per-query cost grows by ~12%, total cost by ~12%. We chose response length deliberately; revisit if eval scores suggest longer responses are needed.
- **Retrieval returns 10 chunks @ ~300 tokens each = 3K input tokens.** If we add a reranker that lets us drop to 5 chunks at higher precision, per-query cost drops ~20%. (See ADR-014 §5 — reranker is a candidate v2 improvement.)
- **Observability cost stays at LangSmith pricing.** If we switch to self-hosted Langfuse, the $0.005 per query disappears (but we add ~$80/month of infra). Crossover at ~16K queries/month — likely a Q4 conversation.

annotations.note: Headline numbers in one block, easy to quote. The CFO will pull these numbers out of the doc; if you don't put them at the top, she'll mis-quote whatever she finds first.

Cost breakdown with each component as a fraction of total. The observability cost being 23% of per-query is the kind of finding that surprises teams — and is the lever the team can pull (self-host) when scale grows.

Usage distribution is the section most rookie analyses skip. Per-user-average is misleading when distribution is right-skewed. The 'top 5 users = 38% of volume' detail matters for capacity planning and for thinking about whether you have a power-user problem or just enthusiastic adopters.

Scaling curve linear through 10× is the kind of statement the CFO wants. The triggers for cost-architecture changes are at specific scales — the team isn't being precious about caching at 40 users, but knows when it'll matter.
Sensitivity analysis on the assumptions whose negation matters. 'If response length grows 30%, cost grows 12%' is the kind of trade-off the team can have a real conversation about with the PO.

common_mistakes: Per-user-per-month calculated from per-user average. If the distribution is right-skewed, the average underestimates total cost. Use the actual distribution.
Cost components rolled up into a single line. The CFO needs to see where the money goes; that's the conversation about what to optimise.
Scaling curve omitted. The CFO is funding for the next 12 months; she wants to know what happens at 5×.
No sensitivity analysis. The cost number looks more certain than it is; surface the assumptions that could move it by 20%+.
Observability cost forgotten. It's typically 10-25% of total inference cost and often missed by junior cost analyses.
Cost stated without naming the model + token assumptions. 'Claude API: $X' isn't reproducible; 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 @ 3K input + 400 output: $X' is.
variant_patterns: Pre-launch variant (no usage data yet): replace §3 with estimated-distribution assumptions. Be honest about the uncertainty range (e.g. '50% confidence interval is $0.50-$2.00/user/month').
Multi-feature variant (multiple AI features sharing infrastructure): components like vector store + observability may be shared. Allocate by query volume share; document the allocation method.

Customer-facing pricing variant: same analysis structure but with margin layered on top. If you're pricing this for end customers, the cost analysis is the floor; the pricing decision is a separate conversation.
